newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Helix drops after Gawler disappointment.
newsitem.headline: Helix drops after Gawler disappointment.

text.p: Shares in gold explorer Helix Resources Ltd dropped as much as 35 cents or 17 percent from an intra-day high of A$2.10 in early afternoon trade after it released new drilling results from its Gawler Craton prospect.
Brokers said the results again disappointed those hoping for signs of a very large gold deposit in the Gawler Craton region.
"The story continues to really be a bit disappointing from the initial expectations," said a broker at Perth brokerage Hartley Poynton.

By 3.05 p.m. (0505 GMT) Helix was down 20 cents on the day to A$1.80, having earlier dropped to A$1.75, just above its low for the year of A$1.65 and well below the A$4.99 touched late last year on the initial Gawler Craton euphoria.
"The grades from the stepped up area look to be pretty low to sub-economic," the Hartley Poynton broker said.
He said the deposit looked to be 500 metres along strike, which would be economic but not enough to justify the A$2.10 price earlier and the A$94 million market capitalisation.

The company earlier said interpretation of the drilling at the Tunkillia Prospect indicated that the 500 metre zone contained a series of narrow high-grade zones ranging from 5.4 g/t to 25.5 g/t over drilled intervals of one to 14 metres.

Major gold miner Acacia Resources Ltd bought a strategic 17 percent stake in Helix in February, paying about A$4.45 per share. Acacia said there was a good chance Helix had found a very large ore body in the Tunkillia Prospect.
"The market's just re-rating it to say 'if they don't find any more then it's not worth the price it was trading at earlier'," said the Perth broker.

Macquarie Equities Ltd analyst Paul Barnes said Helix's price had dropped on disappointment with its quarterly drilling report. The the market had wanted to see more large intervals of low grade mineralisation at the Tunkillia prospect, he said.
"Where we are getting higher grades, they are now quite deep and quite narrow," he told Reuters.
"It is a little bit disappointing," he said, adding however that Helix still had a lot more drilling planned for the year and could still come up with significant results.
Craig Stranger, resource analyst with the Perth-based Todd Partners, said the quarterly lacked any startling news of a large mineable orebody.

"I think the market was hoping for too much too soon," he said, although he believed investors might calm down after publication of the positive outlook by Helix chairman Ewen Tyler at the company's annual meeting.
